# Threads {#sec-threads}

biyos keeps no global state. Everything a call reads or changes belongs to an environment or to a model made on it, so environments are independent of each other. The rule follows:

- Separate threads may use separate environments at the same time, each with its own models.
- One environment is used by one thread at a time, together with every model made on it, except for `BIYOS_interrupt` (@sec-threads-interrupt).

A program that wants to work on one model from several threads copies it onto an environment per thread (@sec-copy). `BIYOS_copymdl` reads the source and changes the target environment, so while it runs no other thread may use either environment. Afterwards the two are apart.

biyos starts no thread of its own yet. `BIYOS_version` reads no state and may be called from any thread. A hook runs on the thread whose call sent the event, so the calls that read or format an event run there too.

## Interrupting a call {#sec-threads-interrupt}

`BIYOS_interrupt` asks the call running on an environment to stop. Any thread may call it while another thread is inside a call on that environment or on one of its models, and so may a signal handler, since it only sets a flag and returns. A long call reads the flag where it checks its time limits and stops with the termination `BIYOS_TRM_STOP`, an outcome rather than an error code. The flag clears when the next call on the environment or on one of its models starts, so a request that arrives after a call has returned does not stop the one that follows. A call made by a hook leaves it set, so a hook may stop the call that sent its event. No call is long enough to read the flag yet.

## In Python {#sec-threads-python}

The package calls the library through `ctypes`, which releases the global interpreter lock for the length of each C call, so threads that work on separate environments run their C code side by side. The rule is the same as in C: one environment, and its models, per thread at a time.

```{.python file="examples/python/threads.py"}
```

Each thread builds its own model on its own environment, and the results come back in the order the work was given, whatever order the threads finished in. A hook written in Python takes the interpreter lock while it runs.

`Env.interrupt` makes the request of @sec-threads-interrupt, and another thread may call it while a call runs. A `KeyboardInterrupt` raised in a hook makes it too, and is raised once the call returns.
